full_judgment:
3. In view of our proposed order it will not be advise able to comment on the factual aspects of the case. It would be sufficient to note the broad facts which are: The petitioner is a businessman and Proprietor of Sandha Bani Cinema Hall at Inderhat, P.S. Sharupkati District Barisal. He has an account being Account No. 638 with Janata Bank, Karikhara Branch. Accused Sultan Hossain was the Manager of the said Branch. On 5-5-75 the petitioner was granted over-draft facility to the tune of Tk. two lacs by the said Branch Manager and the repayment started from 7-5-75 according to terms. The Regional Manager considered that the over-draft facility bad been given by way of violating the Government order and the Bank Rules. He lodged the F.I.R. on 15.5.75 alleging (a) that during 1st demonetization of 100 taka notes accused Sultan Hossain committed gross irregularities and he was suspended from the service of the Bank by order of the Head Office dated 25-4-75 pending enquiry into the matter; (b) in the meantime he disbursed a sum of Tk. 2 lakh to the accused No. 2 (by way of illegal temporary over-draft) "in gross violation of the Bank's Rules and against the credit restriction imposed by the Bangladesh Bank". It was mentioned that the accused Manager did not take any approval from the Head Office or Regional Officer and he, it was alleged "illegally and fraudulently and with intention to defraud the Bank has paid the amount to the accused No. 2 who is a "close friend and business partner" of the accused No. 1. There is a note of interrogation after the word "business partner". However, the allegation was that the accused No. 1 in collusion with the accused petitioner has misappropriated the aforesaid amount and committed criminal breach of trust and further' prejudiced the economic and financial interest of "the State since the Jartata Bank is now fully owned by the Government of Bangladesh and by misappropriating the fund of the Bank; they had in fact, misappropriated the Government fund and thereby affected the economic and financial interest of the state and thus committed an offence under the Special Powers Act, 1974." 

 6. Leave was granted as mentioned above to consider the correctness of the decision. Mr. Moinul Hosein appearing for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is a businessman and the owner of a Cinema Hall. He asked for loan from his Bank, where he had an account. The Manager granted him over-draft facility. The Regional Manger took exception to these and therefore the Bank on 23-5 75 asked for security by way of Mortgage of the Cinema Hall with land and other equipment’s worth over Tk. 5 lacs in favour of the Bank. By 30-1-80, the petitioner had already deposited Tk. 1,01.300/- towards repayment of the loan and interest thereon. The Bank also filed Mortgage Suit being Title Suit No. 60 of 1980 which is pending. In view of the above it is contended that the petitioner had no criminality in the action even if it can be said at the longest that the Bank Manager had sanctioned the over-draft in violation of rules, etc. but that would only be a charge against the Bank Manager. The learned Counsel strenuously argued that how a businessman who in the ordinary course of business takes a loan from the Bank can be liable for criminal prosecution only because he had borrowed money from the Bank by way of over-draft facility. 

 7. The way in which each Bank distributes its fund depends upon the class of business it is doing and the character of deposit. Generally speaking, the deposits of a country bank are more stable than those of a Banker in a large commercial town. A Banker may advance money in one or two ways (i) by allowing his customers over-draft towards his current account, (2) by granting a loan on a separate account. When a banker is asked for a loan, his first enquiry is directed to the possibility of repayment by the borrower and all the Banking Laws and Regulations are directed to the advise ability of advance to trading customers upon a proper valuation of their financial resources and assets. Whenever a security is offered for temporary accommodation the Banker in the usual course of business considers the soundness of the proposal keeping the eye on the over valuation and market fluctuation and the loss which may arise owing to forced sale. In this case the allegation is that the Bank Manager accommodated the petitioner by granting the facility of temporary over-draft since he is a "friend and business partner". It is in the fitness of things that the Bank Manager must know the person thoroughly to whom he is giving facility of over-draft and this relationship arising out of each other's "friendliness" could not be an item in the catalogue of allegation of a criminal action The Manager must know the person to whom he is giving the money and to say to the contrary, is to give a premium to inefficiency, incompetence and malpractice. The petitioner is the owner of Cinema Hall. The moment the objection was taken by the Regional Manager as to the unsecured advance, the Bank by its letter dated 23-5-75 (after 18 days) asked for security by way of mortgage and the petitioner arid his brother took all steps to execute the deed of mortgage. It is true that it took about a year. Mr. Moinul Hosein suggested that those who have something to do with this sort of formalities e.g. execution of document know that for various factors, this is a time-consuming process. Even then the document was executed in May 1976 and by 1980 the Bank had realized more than a lakh with interest. That interest is the profit of the Bank for making the advance. That is how the Bank functions and it exists, amongst others for giving loan and realization of the principal amount plus something extra which is interest. The Regional Manager took exception because the Bank Manager had violated some rules and regulations. That may or may not be. It is a question of evidence. But what would be the charge against the petitioner? At the highest that has been said is that he is friend of the Bank Manager and he is in collusion with the Manager for committing the criminal breach of trust. It is inconceivable how such argument could be made on behalf of the State on the facts of this case. Had it been the case that the petitioner is a man of no means or a person without any ostensible source of income then an argument could be advanced of collusion. A Manager may be taken to task departmentally or by prosecution or both. As a matter of fact, this person was suspended for his performance in connection with the demonetization of notes and the suspension was effective from 24th April, 1975. The allegation of offence under section 477 A has not been made against the petitioner. There is no case against him about falsification of document in connection with demonetized notes. It is the Bank Manager only against whom the charge has been leveled but the petitioner also has been charge-sheeted for which no allegation is even mentioned either in the F.I.R. or in the charge sheet. 

 10. The criminal proceedings, G.R. Case No. 88 of 1975, arose from a First Information Report lodged with the Swarupkati Police Station on 29-5-75 by the Regional Manager of the Sonali Bank against the accused appellant, a businessman and the co-accused, Sultan Hossain, Branch Manager of the Bank at Kawrikhara Bazer on allegation of criminal breach of trust, misappropriation of public 41 money, etc. and charge sheet was submitted against both the accused on 18-7-76 under sections 406, 409 and 477A of the Penal Code, read with Article 16 of the Special Powers Act, 1974 Facts of the case as alleged are that accused, Branch Manager (who is not before us) acting in collusion with the accused-appellant, businessman, disbursed an amount of Taka lacs to the appellant on 5-5-75 apparently by way of as over-draft without however passing any order of sanction and without taking any security whatsoever and that this disbursement being made in total disregard of Government orders, instructions and Bank's Rules & Regulations, prejudicially affected the financial and economic interest of the Bank which is a nationalized financial institution and further that this disbursement constitutes criminal breach of trust and misappropriation. 

 11. Mr. Moinul Hossain, learned Advocate for the appellant, contends that the appellant simply took loan from the Bank and that taking of loan by way of overdraft is a normal business transaction, that adequate security has been furnished subsequently when demanded by the bank authorities and that repayment of the loan has already been Trade to the extent of half of the amount and that this is clearly a civil liability. The learned Advocate further contends that the facts alleged so far as the appellant is concerned, do not constitute any criminal offence and as such continuation of the proceedings is a mere abuse of the Court. Mr. B Hossain learned Assistant Attorney-General, has, on the other hand, contended that when the amount was disbursed to the appellant by the Bank Manager. principal accused, there was no application whatever from the appellant praying for any over-draft or loan nor any order of sanction to the over-draft was made, but the amount was with-drawn from the bank by four cheques of Tk. 50,000/: each, against the account of the appellant whose credit balance was only Tk. 200/- on that day. He has further contended that no security whatever was offered against the over-draft and that this matter was not also reported to the higher authorities, but it was' detected in the course of an inspection by the Regional Manager. This unusual course, it has been further contended, was resorted to by the accused Manager who was the appellant's business partner with whom he acted in collusion. 

 12. Mr. Moinul Hossain has emphasized the fact that though no formal order of sanction for the over-draft was made, the appellant in recognition of the over-draft. started repayment by installment and that proper security was subsequently furnished by executing a deed of mortgage of the appellant's cinema hall and other properties and that for the violation of Rules and Regulations of the Bank the Manager may be responsible but the appellant who got no hand in the matter of observance of the Rules and Regulations cannot be held responsible. It appears that security was furnished more that a year after the disbursement. The question is whether there was any security when the payment was made. Obviously there was none. Criminal breach of trust is constituted, among other things, by disposal of a property held in trust in violation of any direction of law. Charge-sheet has been submitted for alleged commission of a prejudicial act which means any act affecting the economic and financial interests of the State. Moreover, there is a specific allegation of collusion between the accused Manager and the appellant who is said to be the fast friend of the manager and his business partner. These are the matters, now in the form of an allegation, the truth of which can be ascertained only on evidence during trial. In view of these allegations it cannot be said that the facts alleged do not constitute any criminal offence. It is not a fit case for quashing the proceedings as against one of the two accused only.
